exercises.title: Design a Level Editor
exercises.description: Move level definitions into JSON, centralize LevelDef loading and saving, and build a standalone visual editor.
exercises.prompt: Design a level editor for the savetheduckling game.

explanation.summary: This project moves level data into JSON files and adds a standalone pygame editor. The shared LevelDef model now owns both loading and saving, so the game and editor use one JSON schema.

lines.text: Defines the selectable editor tools and the placement tuple associated with each tool.
Builds the same level model used by the game from the objects placed in the editor.
Delegates JSON serialization to level.py so loading and saving stay symmetrical.
Turns left and right mouse clicks into place and erase operations on grid cells.

explanation.run: Run python3 level_editor.py from the project directory.

exercises.title: Add Undo and Redo
exercises.description: Track editor snapshots and support Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y.
exercises.prompt: Implement undo/redo for the level editor.

explanation.summary: The editor records snapshots before every real mutation, enabling conventional Ctrl+Z undo and Ctrl+Y redo without writing separate inverse logic for each tool.

lines.text: Copies the complete lightweight placement dictionary so it can be restored later.
Records the state that existed before a placement or clear operation changed the grid.
Restores the most recent undo snapshot after saving the current state for redo.
Reapplies the most recently undone state when the reader presses Ctrl+Y.

explanation.run: Run python3 level_editor.py and use Ctrl+Z or Ctrl+Y after editing the grid.

exercises.title: Animate a Beatability Pathfinder
exercises.description: Use breadth-first search to test and visualize whether a level is beatable.
exercises.prompt: Create a path finding algorithm for the level editor to test if a level is beatable. Make it animated.

explanation.summary: This module uses breadth-first search to prove that every required target is reachable and supplies visitation/path data for the editor's animated beatability display.

lines.text: Starts breadth-first search with the player position as the first frontier cell.

lines.code: if nxt in came_from or nxt in blocked:
lines.text: Skips cells that were already discovered or cannot be crossed because they contain an obstacle.
Turns the predecessor chain into a route ordered from the current start to the selected goal.

lines.code: goal = reached[0]  # first-reached among remaining == nearest by BFS distance
lines.text: Chooses the nearest remaining target because breadth-first visitation is ordered by path length.

explanation.run: Run python3 level_editor.py and press T after placing the player, siblings, and mother.
